name: Dates
description: Every date from contract start to revenue recognition.
takeaways: Contract start and billing start can differ
Invoice date is an organization-wide rule
Prepaid bills ahead, postpaid in arrears

learn.intro: Seven different dates show up between signing a deal and recognizing revenue. Keep them apart.

cards.title: Contract period
cards.body: Start date and end date of the agreed terms. Charges only exist inside this window.

cards.title: Start billing cycle on (anchor)
cards.body: When invoicing actually begins and which date cycles align to. Defaults to the contract start but can differ. A month-end option makes cycles end on the last day of the month.
cards.example: Contract starts Jan 15, billing cycle starts Feb 1. The first invoice period begins Feb 1.

cards.title: Phase dates
cards.body: Each phase (active, trial or pause) has its own start and end, inside the contract boundaries. A contract needs at least one phase to activate.
cards.example: Trial phase Jan 15 to Feb 13, then a Standard phase from Feb 14. Invoicing starts after the trial ends.

cards.title: Product (line item) dates
cards.body: A product's own start date; its billing cycle starts there unless an anchor date overrides it. Point-in-time products charge per event; period-of-time products charge per period.
cards.example: A seat license (period-of-time) starting Feb 1 bills monthly from Feb 1. An API call (point-in-time) is charged when the event is recorded.

cards.title: Billing period and cadence
cards.body: How often you bill: monthly, quarterly or yearly (ISO 8601 durations P1M, P3M, P1Y), with an offset of prepaid (billed in advance) or postpaid (billed in arrears).
cards.example: P1M prepaid: the March 1 invoice covers March. P1M postpaid: the March 1 invoice covers February.

cards.title: Invoice date
cards.body: By default the generation timestamp (UTC). Optionally derived from generation date, Bill For Date or service period start, then shifted by an offset and pinned to a day.
cards.example: Bill For Date Mar 1, offset +1 month, pinned to last day: invoice dated Apr 30.

cards.title: Revenue recognition date
cards.body: Point-in-time: when the event occurs. Period-of-time: straight-line across the service period. Independent of when you invoice or get paid.
cards.example: A $12,000 annual subscription (period-of-time) is recognized as $1,000 per month. Each API call is recognized the day it happens.

learn.outro: Mental model: contract dates say when the deal is valid, phase and product dates say what applies when, cadence says how often to bill, invoice date says what the paper says, rev rec date says when you earned it.

edgeCases: Contract start ≠ billing start. A contract can begin Jan 15 and start its billing cycle Feb 1. Revenue and invoices follow different clocks here.
Month-end. Bill For Date Mar 1 + 1 month, pinned to last day, gives Apr 30. Service period start Feb 1 pinned to last day gives Feb 28 (Feb 29 in a leap year, handled automatically).
Phases must fit. Phase dates must sit within the contract boundaries; a trial phase delays invoicing until it ends.
Invoice date is not per contract. The rule is organization-wide. One invoice can be edited manually, but only while it is DRAFT.
Open-ended contracts. The newer contract model currently requires an end date, while older docs describe it as optional. Check which version your tenant runs.
Prepaid vs postpaid. Same cadence, different timing: prepaid bills the coming period, postpaid bills the one just finished.

quiz.question: A contract starts Jan 15, but "Start billing cycle on" is Feb 1. When does invoicing begin?
quiz.explanation: The billing cycle start (anchor) is the date invoicing actually begins and can differ from the contract start.

quiz.question: With Invoice Date Configuration off, what date prints on an invoice?
quiz.explanation: The default is the moment Zenskar generated the invoice.

quiz.question: How is revenue recognized for a period-of-time product?
options: At the moment of each event
quiz.explanation: Point-in-time is recognized when the event occurs; period-of-time is recognized uniformly across the period.

quiz.question: When can you manually edit a single invoice's date?
options: Only while the invoice is DRAFT
quiz.explanation: Manual date edits are limited to draft invoices and affect only that invoice.

quiz.question: Which are the phase types on a contract?
quiz.explanation: Draft/active/expired are contract statuses, not phase types.

qa.question: Contract start vs billing anchor?
qa.answer: The contract start is when the agreement begins. The anchor (start billing cycle on) is when invoicing begins and where cycles align.

qa.question: Invoice date vs due date?
qa.answer: The invoice date is what the document says. The due date comes from payment terms, such as Net 30.

qa.question: Prepaid vs postpaid?
qa.answer: Prepaid bills the coming period; postpaid bills the period just finished.

qa.question: Point-in-time vs period-of-time revenue?
qa.answer: Point-in-time is recognized when the event occurs. Period-of-time is recognized straight-line over the service period.

qa.question: Billing period vs service period?
qa.answer: The billing period is what an invoice covers. The service period is when the service is delivered; with postpaid billing they coincide.

qa.question: P1M vs P3M vs P1Y?
qa.answer: ISO 8601 durations for monthly, quarterly and yearly cadence.

qa.question: Generation date vs Bill For Date?
qa.answer: Generation date is when Zenskar created the invoice. Bill For Date is the period date used by the invoice date rule.

qa.question: Phase dates vs contract dates?
qa.answer: Phase dates sit inside contract dates and define when terms apply.

qa.question: Revenue recognition date vs invoice date?
qa.answer: They are independent. Revenue follows performance, invoices follow billing.

qa.question: Same-day vs last-day pinning?
qa.answer: Same day keeps the day number (clamped to month length). Last day always lands on the month's last day.

qa.question: Bill on the last day of every month?
qa.answer: Set the last-day-of-month option on the contract.

qa.question: Align many contracts to one billing date?
qa.answer: Use the same anchor date.

qa.question: Quarterly in arrears with Net 30?
qa.answer: Cadence P3M with postpaid offset, and Net 30 payment terms.

qa.question: Annual prepaid but monthly revenue?
qa.answer: Bill yearly; period-of-time recognition spreads revenue across the months.

qa.question: What happens in February and leap years?
qa.answer: Month-end handling adjusts automatically, so Feb 28 or 29 is used.

qa.question: Anchor on the 31st?
qa.answer: Months with fewer days are clamped to their last day.

qa.question: Can I edit an invoice's date?
qa.answer: Only on a draft invoice, and it affects only that invoice.

qa.question: What time zone is the default invoice date?
qa.answer: UTC generation timestamp.

qa.question: How does Invoice Date Configuration work?
qa.answer: Three steps: pick a reference date, apply an offset, then pin to a day. It is an organization-wide setting.

qa.question: How does pause affect dates?
qa.answer: A pause has a start, an optional resume date and an unpause extension policy. See the API reference for the policy options.
